sources.title: Décision n° 88-60 PDR du 11 mai 1988, Proclamation des résultats de l'élection du Président de la République (Conseil constitutionnel decision page, archived)
sources.rights_note: Factual observations paraphrased with attribution; short quotations only. No photographs, emblems, seals, signatures or long speech text copied. No open license, portrait permission or likeness approval is asserted.
sources.scope_note: The Council's web transcription of decision 88-60 PDR (raw Internet Archive capture of 27 February 2021; the live page is a Drupal render with per-request form tokens). The page cites 'Journal officiel du 12 mai 1988, page 7036', which was not retrieved (Légifrance refuses automated access and no capture was found). Its visa list misdates the 1981 proclamation as 15 May 1988; that visa is not used. The decision precedes the packet period and is recorded because it states the day the second septennat took effect.

claims.text: Decision no. 88-60 PDR of 11 May 1988, deliberated at the sittings of 10 and 11 May 1988, records the second-round results (30 923 249 votes cast; Monsieur François MITTERRAND 16 704 279, Monsieur Jacques CHIRAC 14 218 970) and 'Proclame Monsieur François MITTERRAND Président de la République française'.

locator.section: ground 7 (second-round results) and the operative part ('Proclame ...'); deliberation line
locator.journal_officiel: Journal officiel du 12 mai 1988, page 7036 (cited on the page, not retrieved)

claims.uncertainty: The proclamation of the result, not a start. Web transcription of the decision; the Journal officiel publication was not retrieved.

claims.text: The same decision states: 'Conformément à l'article 6 de la Constitution, le mandat de Monsieur François MITTERRAND prendra effet le 21 mai 1988 à 0 heure.'
claims.uncertainty: A prospective statement dated by the day it was made (11 May 1988); the day it fixes, 21 May 1988 at 0 heure, is the stated start of the second septennat; it lies before the packet period and is a claim only, not the holder's `from`. The Constitution is cited by the Council as its ground; the date is the Council's, not taken from the Constitution's text.

The server's Last-Modified header is generated per request and is not evidence; byte stability rests on identical SHA-256 across the recorded download of 26 September 2026 and this packet's plain and cache-busted downloads of 27-28 September 2026 (UTC). Speaker styling and titles in the archive headings are catalogue labels added later, not part of the original text (the same archive heads Jacques Chirac's election-night declaration of 7 May 1995 'Président de la République' ten days before he took office); dates come from the date line.

claims.text: The Élysée archive publishes François Mitterrand's address 'le jour de son investiture', Palais de l'Élysée, Saturday 21 May 1988; it opens 'Monsieur le Président du Conseil constitutionnel' and interprets 'la volonté populaire exprimée le 8 mai'.

locator.page: 1 (date line and heading) and 2 (salutation and first paragraph)

claims.uncertainty: An investiture ceremony is not itself a start. The heading is a later catalogue label; the day comes from the date line, which is marked 'Seul le prononcé fait foi'.

claims.text: In the address he asks what lesson to draw from 'l'événement qui me vaut d'assumer aujourd'hui, dans la continuité de nos institutions et de mon propre mandat, la magistrature suprême', at the threshold of 'ce septennat'.
claims.uncertainty: The holder's own statement; it supports but never makes a start. 'Aujourd'hui' is dated only by the archive's date line (21 May 1988); it agrees with the effect day the Council stated in advance (fr_cc_88_60_states_mandate_effect_19880511). Marked 'Seul le prononcé fait foi'.

roles.title: Président de la République

holder_claims.name: François Mitterrand
holder_claims.note: Observed on 4 January 1990, the first in-text attestation in the period: at their joint press conference at Latché (Élysée archive transcript) Chancellor Kohl says 'Je suis d'accord avec M. Mitterrand' and speaks of working in 1990 with 'le Président de la République'. The Assemblée nationale's record of 27 August 1990 reads his decree of 22 August 1990 and his message of 27 August 1990, both signed FRANÇOIS MITTERRAND.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: his second septennat began before the packet period; decision 88-60 PDR of 11 May 1988 ('prendra effet le 21 mai 1988 à 0 heure') and his investiture address of 21 May 1988 are claims on the role, not a holder date, as the Brazil, India and South Africa packets date the holder in office when the period opens by an in-period attestation. No end: no source reviewed states, as a record, the day his functions ended. His letter of 16 May 1995 announces the handover for 'Demain matin à onze heures' (prospective), decision 95-81 PDR gives only the outer limit of 21 May 1995 at 0 heure, his successor's address of 17 May 1995 speaks of the fourteen years 'qui viennent de s'écouler' without a day, and the Council's undated 2012 note dating the 1995 handover to 17 May is retrospective; all are claims, and Jacques Chirac's observation of 17 May 1995 is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Jacques Chirac
holder_claims.note: Observed on 17 May 1995: in his address at the Élysée dated that day he says 'En ce jour où je prends la responsabilité d'assumer la plus haute charge de l'Etat', and in his message to the armed forces of the same day he writes 'Président de la République, c'est en tant que chef des Armées que je m'adresse à vous' (Élysée archive).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start: the holder's own same-day statements support but never make a start, and decision 95-81 PDR of 12 May 1995 proclaims him only from the cessation of his predecessor's functions, at the latest 21 May 1995 at 0 heure, without fixing a day; no address of the President of the Council at a 1995 investiture was found. The Council's undated 2012 note and its 2017 dossier table, which date the handover or ceremony to 17 May 1995, are retrospective. The second round (7 May 1995) and the proclamation (12 May 1995) are separate claims, and his letter to Parliament dated 18 May 1995 is a continuation claim. No end: the 2002 decision fixes only the second term's start (17 May 2002 at 0 heure), and the Council's 2012 note computing the first term's end is retrospective.

holder_claims.name: Jacques Chirac
holder_claims.note: From 17 May 2002: the Constitutional Council's decision of 8 May 2002 proclaims M. Jacques CHIRAC President 'à compter du 17 mai 2002 à 0 heure'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is the day fixed in advance by the proclaiming authority; decision 2007-141 PDR repeats it in its visas. The investiture ceremony was held the day before (16 May 2002), when he said of the mandate 'Je l'assumerai', and is a separate claim, as is the election-night declaration of 5 May 2002. No end: his televised declaration of 15 May 2007 announces the transfer of powers for 'Demain' (prospective), decision 2007-141 PDR gives only the outer limit of 16 May 2007 at 24 heures, and the Élysée's biography timeline and the Council's 2012 note are retrospective; Nicolas Sarkozy's start is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Nicolas Sarkozy
holder_claims.note: From 16 May 2007: at the investiture ceremony at the Élysée that day the President of the Constitutional Council told the President of the Republic, identified by his 18.983.138 second-round votes (the total decision 2007-141 PDR gives for M. Nicolas SARKOZY), that he thereby became the sixth President of the Fifth Republic and 'A compter de ce jour, et pour la durée de votre mandat, vous incarnez la France'; his own installation address of that day opens 'En ce jour où je prends officiellement mes fonctions'.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The Council's address names nobody; identity rests on the vote total and on his own address. No hour: the Council's 2007 page puts the ceremony at 11:00, while the Élysée says his predecessor received him at 11:00 before it. The proclamation (10 May 2007), its publication (11 May 2007), the outer limit ('au plus tard, le 16 mai 2007 à 24 heures') and the Élysée's retrospective account of the procès-verbal d'investiture are separate claims. No end: decision 2012-154 PDR gives only the outer limit of 15 May 2012 at 24 heures, and the Council's 2012 note computing the expiry as 16 May 2012 at 0 heure is retrospective; François Hollande's start is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: François Hollande
holder_claims.note: From 15 May 2012: at the investiture ceremony the President of the Constitutional Council told the President of the Republic, identified by his 18 000 668 votes, 'A compter de ce jour, 15 mai 2012, et pour la durée de votre mandat, vous incarnez la France'; the Council's note links this address as Jean-Louis Debré's speech at the investiture of François Hollande, his own declaration of that day opens 'En ce jour où je suis investi de la plus haute charge de l'État', and the Journal officiel prints his decree of 15 May 2012 appointing the Prime Minister, signed François Hollande.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No hour. The proclamation (10 May 2012), its publication (11 May 2012), the outer limit and the handover meeting at 10:00 are separate claims. No end: his interview of 10 May 2017 announces the handover for Sunday 14 May (prospective), decision 2017-171 PDR gives only the outer limit of 14 May 2017 at 24 heures, and the Council's 2017 activity report is retrospective; Emmanuel Macron's start is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: Emmanuel Macron
holder_claims.note: From 14 May 2017: at the investiture ceremony at the Élysée on Sunday 14 May 2017 Laurent Fabius, President of the Constitutional Council, told the President of the Republic, identified by his 20 743 128 second-round votes (the total decision 2017-171 PDR and Fabius's statement of 10 May 2017 give for M. Emmanuel Macron), 'aujourd'hui, en ce dimanche 14 mai, en cet instant précis où vous prenez vos hautes fonctions'. In his investiture address of 7 May 2022 he says the ending mandate began on 14 May 2017.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The Council's address names nobody; identity rests on the vote total. The 2022 statement is retrospective corroboration, not the basis. No hour: the Élysée says his predecessor received him at 10:00 before the ceremony. The proclamation (10 May 2017), its publication (11 May 2017), the outer limit, the Élysée's same-day live-stream notice and the Council's 2017 activity report (retrospective) are separate claims. No end: the 2022 decision fixes only the second term's start (14 May 2022 at 0 heure), and 13 May 2022 is not inferred.

holder_claims.name: Emmanuel Macron
holder_claims.note: From 14 May 2022: decision 2022-197 PDR of 27 April 2022 proclaims M. Emmanuel MACRON President 'à compter du 14 mai 2022 à 0 heure', and Laurent Fabius repeated at the investiture of 7 May 2022 that the second mandate 'débutera le 14 mai à 0 heure'. The Journal officiel prints decrees he signed on 3 and 4 September 2026 (DILA open-data exports), attestations before the cutoff that neither extend nor end the term.
holder_claims.uncertainty: The start is fixed in advance by the proclaiming authority; no record made on 14 May 2022 was reviewed. The first round (9-10 April 2022), the first-round declaration (13 April), the second round (23-24 April), the proclamation (27 April), its publication (28 April) and the investiture (7 May 2022) are separate claims. No end before the 7 September 2026 cutoff.

roles.scope_note: Président de la République under the Constitution of 4 October 1958, recorded as head of state. CLAUDE-C01-23 keeps each election round, the Constitutional Council's declaration of first-round results, its proclamation of the result and the President of the Council's oral announcement of it, the proclamation's publication in the Journal officiel, the handover meeting, the investiture ceremony, a stated start of term, the outer limit the Council states for the predecessor's cessation, the holder's own statements and announcements and his in-office acts as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where the Constitutional Council, in its decision or in its President's address at the investiture, states the day the mandate takes effect or office is taken up, and an end only where a source states the day the office ended; otherwise it is dated by attested_on. A start before the packet period (1 January 1990) is not structured: the holder in office when the period opens is dated by attested_on. The holder's own statement that he assumes office that day supports but never makes a start; a prospective announcement of a handover, an outer limit ('au plus tard'), a successor's statement, a computed expiry and a successor's start are never ends. Retrospective notes, reports, tables and timelines are claims only, and table rows and timeline entries carry no structured date. Élysée archive headings are later catalogue labels. Constitution texts establish procedure only, never a date. No interim presidency (Article 7) is stated for 1990-2026, so none is recorded; acting or interim service would be a claim only, never a holder. Prime ministers, ministers and party offices are outside this role.

unresolved: Presidents 1990-2026 (CLAUDE-C01-23, FR-PRES-01..10) are dated holder observations from the Constitutional Council's decisions, communications and investiture addresses, the Journal officiel (archived Légifrance text pages and DILA open-data exports), the Assemblée nationale's debates and the Élysée's archive. François Mitterrand is dated by attested_on (4 January 1990); the effect day of 21 May 1988 that decision 88-60 PDR states lies before the period and is a claim only. Stated starts: 17 May 2002 (Jacques Chirac), 16 May 2007 (Nicolas Sarkozy), 15 May 2012 (François Hollande), and 14 May 2017 and 14 May 2022 (Emmanuel Macron). Jacques Chirac's 1995 term is dated only by attested_on (17 May 1995): no decision or address of the President of the Council fixes its first day.

No source reviewed states, as a record of the event, the day any President's functions ended, so no holder has an until. The Council states only outer limits ('au plus tard') for 1995, 2007, 2012 and 2017; François Mitterrand (16 May 1995), Jacques Chirac (15 May 2007) and François Hollande (10 May 2017) announced their handovers in advance; the Council's undated 2012 note, its 2017 dossier and activity report and the Élysée's biography timeline are retrospective.

Hours: no source fixes the hour at which any term began. The Council's 2007 page puts the investiture ceremony at 11:00, while the Élysée puts the outgoing President's reception of his successor at 11:00 before it; only days are recorded.

Not retrieved: the Journal officiel publications of the 1988, 1995 and 2002 proclamations (Légifrance refuses automated access and no capture was found), and the published correction (rectificatif) of the 2007 proclamation, JORFTEXT000000465545, whose content could not be read; the Council's 2017 dossier reprints the 2007 dispositif with the same dates.

No interim presidency (Article 7 of the Constitution) is stated for 1 January 1990 to the 7 September 2026 cutoff, so none is recorded; this records the absence of such a statement in the sources reviewed, not a proven absence. Keep executive office distinct from party leadership and from the CNCCFP financial-reporting identities: no organization in this packet is mapped to this institution.
